title: Discovery of the cosmic microwave background
summary: In 1964 Arno Penzias and Robert Wilson of Bell Laboratories at Holmdel, New Jersey, found microwaves with a wavelength of about 7 centimeters that were stronger than expected. NASA says the discovery was made more or less by accident and matched a temperature of 3.5 kelvin from empty space. Scientists at nearby Princeton University identified the radiation as a remnant of the Big Bang, and the pair received the 1978 Nobel Prize in Physics.

uncertainty.note: Penzias and Wilson detected the isotropic microwave excess during observations in 1964 and published their joint letter with Dicke's Princeton team in July 1965 in the Astrophysical Journal.

importance.justification: NASA says the discovery provided the first observational evidence that the universe started with a Big Bang, and the Nobel Prize in Physics 1978 was awarded for it.

related.because: CMB observations and space telescope measurements jointly constrained the Hubble constant, cosmic expansion rate, and cosmological parameters.

beats.caption: At Crawford Hill in Holmdel, New Jersey, Arno Penzias and Robert Wilson detect an unexplained isotropic microwave hiss.
The radiation is identified as relic heat from the creation of the universe, establishing observational proof of the Big Bang.
